accounting.rationale: Informative note explaining that intrinsic operator symbols can be used as defined-operation operators and thereby extend generic properties; the normative extension requirements are accounted under p4-p6 and 15.4.3.4.2.
Informative restatement of intrinsic operator extension; no independent requirement or coverage claim is created.

requirements.title: A unary defined operation is established by an applicable one-argument function and generic operator interface
requirements.definition: A unary defined operation has the form defined-unary-op x2 or intrinsic-operator x2 and is defined only when a one-dummy FUNCTION or ENTRY is supplied through an OPERATOR generic interface or corresponding type-bound generic binding, with dummy type, type parameters, rank or elemental rank route, and array shape satisfying the stated operand conditions.

pending.unary-defined-operation-forms: PENDING source-only positive controls for both defined-unary-op x and intrinsic-operator x forms, using a derived operand and an independently computed function-result value. Grammar ownership remains 10.1.2.4/R1004 and intrinsic operator tokens remain their 10.1.2 owners.
pending.one-dummy-function-definition: PENDING source shape with a FUNCTION and an ENTRY-specific companion considered separately, each exposing exactly one nonoptional dummy data object through a valid OPERATOR generic. Arity interface restrictions remain dependencies on 15.4.3.4.2.
pending.operator-generic-interface-route: PENDING module generic interface OPERATOR(.u.) binding a one-dummy function; the oracle compares the operation result with a direct call result without relying on evaluation order.
pending.type-bound-generic-binding-route: PENDING derived type with a specific binding and GENERIC :: OPERATOR(.u.) => binding. Controls distinguish declared type availability from dynamic type corresponding-binding selection without testing generic-resolution machinery as this requirement.
pending.dummy-compatible-with-dynamic-operand-ty: PENDING positive/negative source contrast using a declared polymorphic operand whose dynamic type is compatible with the dummy in the valid case. An incompatible companion must be otherwise well formed and attributed here only if generic resolution is not already invalid under 15.4.3.4.5.
pending.dummy-type-parameters-match-operand: PENDING source plan with parameterized derived operands where kind/len parameters match in the valid case and differ in an isolated companion; future diagnostics must not be counted if the type definition itself violates 7.5 parameter rules.
pending.specific-rank-match: PENDING non-elemental unary function plans for scalar and rank-one operands where operand and dummy ranks match; a mismatched-rank companion must not be confused with array shape conformance.
pending.elemental-no-other-function-rank-route: PENDING elemental one-dummy function plan demonstrating the rank route only when no other function defines the operation. A companion with a competing applicable specific belongs to generic distinguishability/applicability dependencies, not to an execution oracle.
pending.unary-array-shape-match: PENDING explicit-shape dummy and conforming operand source plans, plus a shape-mismatch restriction plan if a safe compile-time shape contrast can isolate p3 without relying on undefined execution.
pending.intrinsic-unary-operator-extension: PENDING defined extension of a unary intrinsic operator such as .NOT. for a derived type, using operand/result components with literal values. Intrinsic logical interpretation remains 10.1.5.4; this facet owns only the defined-operation route.

requirements.oracle: Future positives compare the operation value with the defining function result for literal-bearing operands. Future negatives must isolate the p2/p3 applicability condition and not an OPERATOR interface constraint, grammar error, generic ambiguity, or unsupported dynamic-type feature.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future cases must not infer which operand was evaluated, the order of evaluation, or whether an optional evaluation was omitted; must not assert a result that a permitted mathematically or logically equivalent rewrite could change; must not use floating-point tolerance as an escape hatch; must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly, or undefined reads; and must attribute every negative to the cited requirement rather than to an independently invalid rule owned elsewhere.

requirements.title: A binary defined operation is established by an applicable two-argument function and generic operator interface
requirements.definition: A binary defined operation has the form x1 defined-binary-op x2 or x1 intrinsic-operator x2 and is defined only when a two-dummy FUNCTION or ENTRY is supplied through an OPERATOR generic interface or a corresponding type-bound generic binding in the declared and dynamic type of either operand, with dummy type, type parameters, ranks or elemental conformability route, and array shapes satisfying the stated conditions. Intrinsic operator symbols can be extended by such defined operations.

pending.binary-defined-operation-forms: PENDING source-only positive controls for x defined-binary-op y and x intrinsic-operator y forms, with a derived result component equal to an independently computed literal. Syntax is owned by 10.1.2.9/R1023-R1024 and intrinsic operator grammar by 10.1.2.
pending.two-dummy-function-definition: PENDING FUNCTION and ENTRY source shapes whose defining procedure has exactly two dummy arguments d1 and d2. Arity constraints on OPERATOR interfaces remain owned by 15.4.3.4.2.
pending.operator-generic-interface-route: PENDING module INTERFACE OPERATOR(.b.) route binding a two-dummy function and comparing x .b. y with the direct function result under the same arguments.
pending.type-bound-generic-binding-route-left-or: PENDING type-bound GENERIC OPERATOR route where the generic binding is in the declared type of the left operand in one control and the right operand in another, and a corresponding binding exists in the selected dynamic type.
pending.dummies-compatible-with-dynamic-operand-: PENDING polymorphic left/right operand controls where d1 and d2 are compatible with the dynamic types of x1 and x2 respectively; any rejection must not already be caused by an inaccessible procedure or non-distinguishable generic pair.
pending.dummy-type-parameters-match-operands: PENDING parameterized derived-type binary operation controls with matching type parameters for both operands and isolated mismatches for each side. Parameter declaration validity remains a 7.5 dependency.
pending.specific-rank-matches: PENDING non-elemental scalar/rank-one binary operation controls where both operand ranks match their corresponding dummies; a rank mismatch plan must identify the failing side and avoid shape-mismatch misattribution.
pending.elemental-conformable-no-other-function-: PENDING elemental two-dummy function controls for conformable array operands when no other function defines the operation. Do not infer anything from element evaluation order, simultaneity, or omission.
pending.binary-array-shape-match: PENDING explicit-shape array dummy controls requiring x1 and x2 shapes to match d1 and d2 respectively when either dummy is an array. Repairs change only the shape that is under test.
pending.intrinsic-binary-operator-extension: PENDING defined extension of an intrinsic binary operator for a derived type with operand types/kinds/ranks differing from intrinsic operations, preserving 15.4.3.4.2 interface constraints.
pending.concat-defined-extension-grouping-contro: PENDING grouping source plan delegated by 10.1.2.6: define OPERATOR(//) for a derived type carrying an integer component, with result value left%v*10+right%v. Operands with literal values 1, 2, and 3 distinguish (a//b)//c = 123 from a//(b//c) = 33; both parenthesisations have independently computed expectations and valid interfaces.
pending.and-defined-extension-grouping-control: PENDING grouping source plan delegated by 10.1.2.8: define OPERATOR(.AND.) for the same kind of derived literal-bearing type, returning a derived value such as left%v*10+right%v. This makes grouping value-observable without observing short-circuiting or operand evaluation paths.
pending.eqv-neqv-defined-extension-grouping-cont: PENDING grouping source plan delegated by 10.1.2.8: define OPERATOR(.EQV.) and/or OPERATOR(.NEQV.) for derived operands with non-associative component results, compare the unparenthesized left-recursive chain with the explicitly right-parenthesized chain, and avoid truth-table or side-effect oracles.
pending.generic-nonapplicability-not-syntax: PENDING diagnostic attribution plan for a syntactically valid defined-binary expression whose second operation has no applicable defining function. The negative is filed here or under 15.4.3.4.2/15.4.3.4.5, not under 10.1.2.9 R1023 syntax.

requirements.oracle: Future grouping-sensitive controls use derived operands and non-associative result components so the oracle is a value comparison between independently computed parenthesisations, never a side-effect, call-count, operand-order, short-circuit, or compiler-agreement observation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future cases must not infer which operand was evaluated, the order of evaluation, or whether an optional evaluation was omitted; must not assert a result that a permitted mathematically or logically equivalent rewrite could change; must not use floating-point tolerance as an escape hatch; must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly, or undefined reads; and must attribute every negative to the cited requirement rather than to an independently invalid rule owned elsewhere.

review_rationale: batch103: independent fresh-context source review against pinned J3/24-007 (sha256 7371e889...). Reviewer read all 20 base units of 10.1.6.1, 10.1.6.2, 10.1.6.3, 10.1.7 and 10.1.8 in the original PDF rather than the author summary, verified 20 base / 56 fine units, 10 requirements and 63 facets (all pending), and separately re-read the 10.1.2.4, 10.1.2.6, 10.1.2.8 and 10.1.2.9 grammar units to confirm ownership. A global name-head check over 502 rule heads found 0 missing, 0 duplicate and 0 unmatched, and confirmed the defined-operator grammar owners remain R1004/C1005, R1024/C1006, R1012, R1020 and R1022. Every processor freedom is correctly recorded as a permission: 10.1.6.3 p1 equivalent-expression latitude is bounded by parenthesis integrity, 10.1.7 p1 records that a processor need not evaluate all operands or evaluate each entirely, and 10.1.8 p1 keeps the rewrite context as permission while preserving the normative requirement that a parenthesized expression be treated as a data entity. 10.1.7 p3 is the single restriction in scope, with its CRITICAL and END CRITICAL exceptions. This packet carries four delegations left open by earlier batches: defined-binary applicability and generic nonapplicability from 10.1.2.9, and the left-recursive grouping facets from 10.1.2.6 and 10.1.2.8, which are discharged through a value-observable non-associative defined extension rather than through truth tables, short-circuiting or side effects. Undefined-status effects are recorded as not value-observable by reading the entity, and finite samples are recorded as able to refute but never to prove the all-possible-primary-values equivalence of 10.1.6.3 p2. Decision: accept, no blocking findings; three non-blocking observations recorded in doc/source_audits/batch_103.json. This registers source accounting only: it is not fixture approval, it supplies no execution, and it approves no oracle.
